problem.title: The Frontend Paradox of Web 3.0
problem.text: Modern decentralized applications suffer from a fatal architectural contradiction. Smart contracts and tokens reside on decentralized blockchains, but the user interfaces through which humans interact with them are hosted on centralized infrastructure - AWS, Cloudflare, Vercel, Google Cloud. A single court order, a single provider's terms-of-service violation, or a single government firewall can erase any 'decentralized' application from the global internet. The frontend is the single point of failure.
problem.b1: Centralized hosting = single point of failure
problem.b3: No economic incentives for long-term availability

solution.title: Netfory: Autonomous Web 4.0 Infrastructure
solution.text: Netfory replaces the centralized hosting stack with a decentralized, content-addressed distribution network powered by the Iroh (QUIC) transport layer and BLAKE3 cryptographic verification. Through a native Proof-of-Utility economic model, network participants (seeders) are directly compensated in STH for providing storage and bandwidth.
solution.callout: The network is not managed by agents. The network IS the decentralized agents. Netfory is the operating system of the Decentralized Physical Internet. Every desktop client is an autonomous node that discovers peers, verifies content, and sustains the economy. Your device doesn't just access the web. It is the web.

architecture.title: System Architecture

formulas.title: The Four Formulas of Web 4.0
formulas.c1x: Access is a matter of connecting to a protocol (sn://, u://, sth://, dev://, api://), not having permission on a server. No server can deny access. No API key can be revoked. The protocol is the law.
formulas.c2x: State exists distributed in the network. The user does not 'download' a page; they synchronize state via P2P. There is no single source of truth - the truth is distributed.
formulas.c3x: No AWS, no Google Cloud, no Vercel. All backend logic - databases, APIs, load balancers - migrates to the P2P protocol layer. No corporation can deplatform an application.
formulas.c4x: Everything is bound to a Content Identifier (CID), computed via BLAKE3. Content proves itself. No domain can be seized. No certificate can be revoked. Content is immortal.

economics.title: Money as Anti-Spam and Motivation
economics.text: The native coin STH (SmartHoldem) is integrated directly into the protocol as both fuel and anti-spam shield. Every action that consumes network resources costs a small amount of STH. This makes spam economically devastating for attackers while simultaneously creating a perpetual revenue stream for honest participants.
economics.f1ex: For N = 1,000,000 messages at 0.01 STH each, the attacker burns 10,000 STH - a provably irrational expenditure.
economics.f2ex: A seeder with Base=5, seededGb=100, density=0.5, activeApps=10, PerApp=0.2, K_up=1.0 earns 57 STH/day = 20,805 STH/year.

speed.title: Built for Speed and Scale
speed.text: SmartHoldem's new Rust core breaks traditional blockchain limits: Node.js and PostgreSQL bottlenecks are replaced with an optimized engine and Sled DB, delivering lightning-fast sync and massive throughput.
speed.c1x: Blocks of 500 transactions are verified and applied in ~50 ms. Powered by a BFT finality gadget and parallel processing, the network achieves absolute, irreversible finality in just 1 slot (~8 seconds).
speed.c2x: Powered by the Iroh P2P protocol. No centralized cloud providers needed, but you can run your own node. Any laptop, Raspberry Pi, or ARM64 mobile device can be a full, validating node behind any NAT, without a static IP.
speed.c3x: A full validating node now runs on just ~800 MB of RAM. DPoS combined with Rust's zero-cost abstractions makes this the most energy-efficient networks in existence.

stack.title: Technical Stack
stack.c1l1x: 100% Rust with parallel signature verification (Rayon), memory safety and zero-cost abstractions.
stack.c1l2x: Embedded Sled key-value store with zstd compression = 11.7M+ blocks in ~8 GB, replacing legacy PostgreSQL dependencies.
stack.c1l3x: DPoS with 21 active delegates, enhanced by a BFT finality gadget (deterministic finality in 1 slot).
stack.c1l4x: Hybrid security model. Classic secp256k1 (BIP-Schnorr) + post-quantum ML-DSA-44 (NIST FIPS 204) via Quantum Shield.
stack.c2l1x: Native window.smartholdem IPC for Tauri dApps. Secure, sandboxed access to signing, P2P storage, and network state.
stack.c2l2x: Native SmartObjects & Tokens. Registries, issuance, zero smart-contract overhead and no EVM risks.
stack.c2l3x: BLAKE3 content-addressed verification. Metadata anchored on-chain in SmartNetData, absolute integrity, with no external indexers.
stack.c2l4x: 100% backward-compatible RESTful API + SDK. Real-time QUIC push streams for instant, polling-free updates.
stack.c3l1x: Built on Iroh (QUIC/UDP), providing encrypted, multiplexed connections with native NAT traversal and hole-punching. Nodes can produce and sync blocks from behind home routers without a static IP.
stack.c3l2x: Dual-stack architecture. Primary communication occurs over the decentralized Iroh mesh, while a legacy WebSocket/Protobuf bridge (port 4001) is maintained strictly for backward compatibility with nodes on servers.
stack.c3l3x: Peer discovery relies on Mainline DHT, local mDNS, and a cryptographically signed Peer Address Book, eliminating any dependency on centralized DNS or public relay services.

decentral.p1x: Validators are chosen based on reputation, not centralized control.
decentral.p2x: Users vote with the power of their balance. Coins remain under complete user control.
decentral.p3x: Any STH holder can vote, elect, or cancel delegates. Ineffective delegates are swiftly replaced by the community.

top21.title: The TOP 21: Securing the Network
top21.text: Delegates (also known as witnesses or block producers) are responsible for verifying transactions, creating new blocks, and protecting the SmartHoldem network. They cannot alter or influence transaction data.
top21.note: The delegation system is highly competitive. A delegate can move into or out of the TOP 21 at any time. This sustainable scheme provides an opportunity for new delegates to prove themselves and attract the community's attention.

quantum.title: SmartHoldem Quantum Shield
quantum.subtitle: How We Protect the Blockchain from Future Computers
quantum.text: While the market discusses charts, a threat capable of nullifying classical cryptography is maturing. Shor's algorithm on a sufficiently powerful quantum computer could break ECDSA — the mathematical foundation of most blockchains today. SmartHoldem is not waiting for a hypothetical 'Day X'.
quantum.callout: {waiting} Stage A (Post-Quantum Key Commitments) is already ACTIVE in the mainnet.
quantum.waitingLabel: We are building the shield today.

phases.title: Implementation Plan: Hybrid Model
phases.text: We rule out abrupt hard forks and forced mass migrations. The transition to quantum resilience is gradual, seamless, and backward-compatible:
phases.p1b1: Users can already anchor the SHA-256 hash of their future ML-DSA-44 public key via the vendorField (sthpq1:...).
phases.p1b2: This prevents 'race condition' attacks when Phase 2 activates, securing the wallet before the quantum threat materializes.
phases.p2b1: Users can register a post-quantum ML-DSA-44 public key (NIST FIPS 204) as a second signature on their existing wallet.
phases.p2b2: From that moment, every transaction requires two signatures: the classic secp256k1 one and the new quantum-resistant one.
phases.p2b3: The classic key stays active for full compatibility, while the post-quantum key adds a quantum-resistant second layer — forming a robust hybrid scheme that protects your assets even if either algorithm is compromised.
phases.p3b1: All 21 active delegates sign blocks with post-quantum signatures to prevent consensus spoofing.
phases.p3b2: The Iroh P2P transport layer uses hybrid key exchange (X25519 + ML-KEM-768) to secure messenger and dApp data (SHIP-40).

sig.title: Upgrade the Lock, Not the Vault
sig.text: Unlike other networks that require users to create new wallets and mass-transfer assets, SmartHoldem leverages its unique second-signature architecture for a seamless quantum upgrade.
sig.s1x: Your SmartHoldem address is derived from your classic secp256k1 public key. This remains unchanged.
sig.s2x: You register your post-quantum ML-DSA-44 public key as a second signature on your existing address.
sig.s3x: Every transaction now requires both the classic and the post-quantum signature to be valid.
sig.r1: You do not need to change your wallet or address
sig.r2: Your coins stay exactly where they have been for years
sig.r4: Your account is now protected by a dual cryptographic layer
sig.r5: Even if a quantum computer derives your first private key, it cannot move your funds without the valid second (quantum-resistant) signature
sig.footer: {forUsers} You can activate a second signature at any time to instantly enable quantum protection, or migrate to new quantum-safe address types in the distant future.
sig.forUsersLabel: For users on a single signature:

nuance.title: Technical Nuances & Network Protection
nuance.n1b1: In a DPoS network, delegates sign blocks
nuance.n1b2: Compromised delegate signatures threaten the entire blockchain's integrity
nuance.n1b3: Implementing PQC at the protocol level makes SmartHoldem a "digital fortress" resistant to consensus spoofing
nuance.n2b1: We selected ML-DSA-44 (NIST FIPS 204) for its optimal balance: ~2.4 kB signatures and sub-millisecond verification
nuance.n2b2: The Rust core's parallel processing (Rayon) ensures these heavy transactions are verified instantly without losing sync speed
nuance.n3b1: The protocol includes an alg_id byte in PQC objects
nuance.n3b2: This allows seamless future upgrades (e.g., to FN-DSA-512 / Falcon) without requiring users to change addresses or migrate funds
nuance.n3b3: For the user, this looks like a familiar wallet

hero.title: The Web 4.0 Protocol: A Breakthrough for Humanity
hero.subtitle: Our mission is to enhance the internet by developing the Netfory OS, Web4 infrastructure, and foundational technologies that promote human autonomy.
hero.quote: Netfory is the operating system of the Decentralized Physical Internet. No central server. No corporate control. Just code, cryptography, and you.

deplatform.p1: In hostile environments, freedom of speech and information distribution are the first rights to be restricted. Centralized platforms can erase voices with a single click.
deplatform.p3: Large-scale content removal or blocking operations fail because content is preserved across decentralized networks. Deplatforming is no longer a viable, low-cost tool of control. Freedom of expression shifts from platform tolerance to network resilience.
deplatform.p4: Reliable messaging, publishing, and social graph infrastructure become the default. Content survives as long as at least one peer holds it. This is the infrastructure of the Decentralized Physical Internet. By removing central points of failure, Netfory makes deplatforming a thing of the past.

archives.subtitle: Solving the Long-Term Memory Crisis
archives.p1: How do we preserve journalistic investigations, scientific records, and the documentation of civil society? In Web 2.0 and Web 3.0, a server shutdown means history is erased.
archives.p2Bold: Netfory solves the problem of long-term storage.
archives.p3: Through content-addressable architecture, archives of journalism, science, and civic memory are permanently preserved. As long as the information exists on at least one peer in the network, it cannot be destroyed.

impact.subtitle: We don't just build technology. We measure its real-world impact on human freedom.
impact.m1Text: Volume of journalistic, scientific, and civic memory permanently stored and instantly searchable on content-addressable infrastructure.
impact.m2Text: Number of developers publishing uncensorable dApps and repositories directly to the P2P network, free from centralized platform bans.

lanFirst.titleB: : Survival When the World Goes Dark
lanFirst.p1: In a world of fiber cuts, regional blackouts, and internet isolation, traditional networks fail. Clearnet and IPFS rely on global routing. If the cable is cut, they die.
lanFirst.p2Bold: Netfory is different. It is built with a true LAN-First architecture.
lanFirst.p3: When the global connection drops, Netfory clients don't panic. They automatically switch to local peer discovery via **mDNS**. Your local network becomes a sovereign island:
lanFirst.b1: **E2EE Chats** continue to work between neighbors or colleagues in the same building or street.
lanFirst.b2: **File Sharing** via CID operates at lightning speed within the local cluster.
lanFirst.b3: **Cached dApps** stay fully functional without a single request to the outside world.
lanFirst.closing: We are not just building an alternative internet. We are building a **digital lifeboat** that keeps knowledge, communication, and community alive when everything else goes silent.

faq.q1: What is Web 4.0 and how does Netfory implement it?
faq.a1: Web 4.0 is a serverless, autonomous internet where applications live directly on user devices without central hosting. Netfory implements it as a peer-to-peer network on top of the SmartHoldem (STH) blockchain: applications are content-addressed, run natively on peers, and require no cloud infrastructure.
faq.a2: LAN-First is a Netfory paradigm where clients automatically fall back to local peer discovery via mDNS when the global internet is unavailable. When the WAN link is cut, E2EE chats still work between neighbors, CID-based file sharing operates at LAN speed, and cached dApps stay fully functional — all with zero dependency on external routing.
faq.q3: How is Netfory different from IPFS or Clearnet?
faq.a3: Clearnet and IPFS rely on global routing; if the cable is cut they stop working. Netfory is built with a true LAN-First architecture and switches to mDNS peer discovery on the local network the moment global connectivity drops, keeping communication and file sharing alive.
faq.q4: Does Netfory require a central server?
faq.a4: No. Netfory has zero central servers. All data, messages and applications travel peer-to-peer over the Iroh/QUIC transport, with content addressed by CID and identities anchored to on-chain SmartHoldem wallets.
faq.a5: No. There is no central authority that can delete content from the network. Filters exist only at the storefront/discovery layer as opt-in reputation badges — direct sn:// and sth:// links always work regardless of any list.

hero.title: Reputation Over Censorship: How Netfory Ensures Safety Without Central Control
hero.subtitle: In Real Web4, safety doesn’t come from bans. It comes from reputation and user choice.

dilemma.title: The Open Network Dilemma
dilemma.p1: Any open Peer-to-Peer network faces the same hard choice: total openness creates space for scams and phishing. Centralized moderation destroys decentralization and creates a single point of control.
dilemma.p2: SmartNet Web4 protocols solve this differently. We don’t ban. We use decentralized reputation.
dilemma.p3: A simple two-tier catalog system (Official {'|'} All) protects everyday users by default, while leaving the network completely free for those who want full access. We mark, we don’t censor.

catalog.l1Intro: Ordinary users in USER mode see only verified dApps. An app is Official if:
catalog.l1B1: Signed by a Trusted Developer: The manifest includes an owner address in the community-vetted DEVELOPERS registry. Cryptographic signatures make affiliation impossible to fake.
catalog.l1B2: Approved by Governance: Specific app IDs can be added to OFFICIAL_DAPPS via public blockchain transaction.
catalog.l1Note: This is a mathematically verifiable reputation badge, not a corporate ban list.
catalog.l2Text: Advanced users in DEV/GEEK modes can toggle “Show Unverified” with a clear warning. The network hides nothing from those who understand the risks.

transport.title: Direct Links Always Work
transport.p1: This is a core principle of SmartNet Web 4.0 protocols: We mark. We never censor. Direct links using sn:// or sth:// protocols are never blocked — under any circumstances. If you receive a link from a peer, it opens regardless of official lists.
transport.p2: Filters apply ONLY to storefront discovery, never to the underlying transport layer. The network itself remains fully open.

decentral.title: Decentralized Safety Mechanics
decentral.r1d: Trackers index ALL apps. “Official” is just a visibility metadata tag.
decentral.r2d: Trust registries live on the SmartHoldem Blockchain. Immutable and public.
decentral.r3d: Filtering happens locally on your device. Forking the client, switching to GEEK mode, or using a direct link bypasses all filters. The network cannot force a filter onto your node.
decentral.r4d: Badges are verified via signed manifests (id ↔ pubkey + owner). You verify the signature yourself.
decentral.note: Unlike traditional app stores, there are no hidden algorithms or backdoors.

vdapps.title: Safety Even Without Internet Access
vdapps.p1: For users in hostile networks or offline segments, SmartNet uses Cloud Seeders. Trusted developers replicate encrypted state files (vdapps.enc) containing current trust lists every 30 minutes.
vdapps.p2: Peers only accept these lists if the issuer is already in their known DEVELOPERS set. This creates a transitive chain of trust anchored in the initial configuration. Man-in-the-middle attacks are impossible because unknown issuers are automatically ignored.

final.title: Web4 Safety for a Free Internet
final.p1: Reputation instead of censorship. Signatures instead of promises. Choice instead of prohibition.
final.p2: Everyday users are protected by default. Advanced users keep full visibility.
final.p3: And no one in the world has a button that can delete an application from the network.

faq.q1: How does SmartNet ensure safety without censorship?

faq.q2: Can SmartHoldem delete an app from the network?
faq.a2: No. Content is never deleted from the network. Trackers index all apps and the Official flag is only a visibility metadata tag stored on the SmartHoldem blockchain. Filtering happens locally on the user device and can be bypassed by forking the client or using a direct sn:// link.
faq.q3: Do sn:// or sth:// direct links ever get blocked?
faq.a3: Never. Direct links using sn:// or sth:// protocols always resolve regardless of any list. Filters apply only to storefront discovery, never to the underlying transport layer.
faq.a4: Every Official app has a signed manifest binding its id to a pubkey and owner address. The client verifies the signature locally against the on-chain DEVELOPERS registry — spoofing is mathematically impossible.
faq.q5: How does safety work when the user is offline?
faq.a5: SmartNet uses Cloud Seeders. Trusted developers replicate encrypted vdapps.enc state files with current trust lists every 30 minutes. Peers only accept these lists if the issuer is already in their known DEVELOPERS set, creating a transitive chain of trust anchored in the initial configuration.

hero.title: Messaging Without Witnesses: The Web 4.0 Standard
hero.subtitle: Nobody Can See Who You Talk To. Privacy is a human right secured by mathematics.

messenger.title: Decentralized Messaging: No Servers. No Logs.
messenger.p1: Traditional messengers rely on centralized servers that store your metadata and scan your content. SmartNet’s P2P Messenger eliminates the middleman completely.
messenger.b1: Direct Device-to-Device: Messages travel via Iroh (QUIC) straight from your device to your peer. No servers. No MITM.
messenger.b2: E2EE by Default: Every message is encrypted with X25519 + AES-256-GCM. Only the recipient can decrypt it.
messenger.b3: Group Sovereignty: Create groups with admin-controlled policies. Kick members, rotate keys, set entry fees — all enforced by cryptography, not server rules.
messenger.b4: Anti-Spam Economics: Set a price for incoming messages. Spammers must pay STH to reach you. Mass harassment becomes economically impossible.

mail.title: 0xID Mail: Three Levels of Privacy. One Client.
mail.p1: Why choose between convenience and security? 0xID Mail works with your existing Gmail or Yandex accounts while offering military-grade encryption and blockchain-verified identity.
mail.m1Text: Use it as your daily driver. Connect any IMAP/SMTP account. All history stays in a local, PIN-encrypted Sled database.
mail.m2Text: Send fully encrypted emails to any normal email address. The provider only sees Base64 garbage. Your identity is verified on-chain with a green Verified Badge — spoofing becomes impossible.
mail.m3Text: Total anonymity. No SMTP servers. No logs. Messages travel directly via Iroh P2P. Addresses like alice{'@'}sth are registered on-chain and belong to you forever.

antispam.title: Economic Anti-Spam & Cryptographic Identity
antispam.p1: In Web 4.0, money is the ultimate anti-spam shield. To message a new contact, you send a small Invite Transaction (1 STH). This proves you are a real human, not a bot farm.
antispam.p2: Every sender’s identity is cryptographically tied to their SmartHoldem wallet. If someone tries to spoof an address, the client checks the blockchain signature instantly.

tech.title: Under the Hood: Zero-Trust Architecture
tech.r1d: All emails and chats live in an encrypted Sled DB on your device. Lost PIN = Lost Data. This is a feature.
tech.r2d: Your address book exists only on your device. No server knows who you talk to.
tech.r4d: If the recipient is offline, the client automatically falls back to an encrypted envelope via SMTP (Mode 2).

final.title: Your Data. Your Keys. Your Network.
final.p1: Stop renting privacy from Big Tech. Start owning it.

faq.q1: Does the Netfory messenger use any central server?
faq.a1: No. Messages travel device-to-device via the Iroh transport over QUIC. There is no central server, no message broker, and no metadata store. Nobody can see who talks to whom.
faq.a2: Every message is encrypted by default with X25519 key exchange and AES-256-GCM authenticated encryption. Only the recipient device holds the private key needed to decrypt.
faq.q3: What is 0xID Mail and how is it different from Gmail?
faq.a3: 0xID Mail is a mail client with three privacy modes. Mode 1 is a classic IMAP/SMTP client with local PIN-encrypted Sled storage. Mode 2 sends fully encrypted mail through normal SMTP with an on-chain Verified Badge that makes address spoofing mathematically impossible. Mode 3 is pure P2P over Iroh with alice{'@'}sth addresses registered on-chain — no SMTP servers, no logs.
faq.a4: To message a new contact you send a small Invite Transaction (1 STH), which proves you are a real human rather than a bot farm. Recipients can also set a per-message price, forcing spammers to pay STH to reach them and making mass harassment economically infeasible.
faq.q5: What happens if the recipient is offline?
faq.a5: The client automatically falls back to an encrypted envelope over SMTP (Mode 2). The recipient sees a normal-looking email in any provider, decrypts it locally with their key, and the message never touches the Netfory storefront.
